citations.quote: the asset will be misvalued: overvalued if the signal is good and undervalued if it is bad.
the tendency, driven by a desire to maintain a positive self-image, to give oneself credit for a good outcome but to blame a bad outcome on extraneous bad luck.
Biased updating of this kind generates both medium-term momentum and
the very high trading volume in financial markets

frontmatter_snapshot.summary: Daniel-Hirshleifer-Subrahmanyam: overconfident investors overweight private signals, causing mispricing that corrects on public news (excess volatility, reversal); adding biased self-attribution -- confidence rising on confirming public news but not falling on disconfirming news -- produces short-run momentum then long-run reversal.
frontmatter_snapshot.title: Overconfidence and Biased Self-Attribution in Prices
